situation:
You are the training coordinator at WILLOW AND VINE FLORISTS, a group of eleven shops formed eight months ago when two family florists merged. The managing director (judge) has asked you to recommend how the twenty designers hired for the holiday season will be trained, with the first of them starting in three weeks.

The MARLOWE STREET FLOWERS shops that came in with the merger sell on a promise printed on every card: each arrangement is made the day it is delivered by the designer who signs it. Those designers were taught over six weeks beside a senior designer. The shops on the other side of the merger work from central recipe cards.

A two-day online module and a set of recipe cards would have every shop staffed before the first holiday orders, and costs a fraction of the six-week apprenticeship. It would also put new designers' signatures on cards for work they were coached through. The six-week course keeps senior designers off the bench through the group's busiest weeks.

The managing director (judge) wants you to recommend one training plan and to say how it will be explained to the senior designers whose shops it changes. You will present in the managing director's (judge) office. The managing director (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you for your work after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the managing director (judge) of WILLOW AND VINE FLORISTS. Business background is the same as the situation above. Eight months after the merger the two halves of the group still train differently, and the holiday season will not wait for that to settle itself.

You want the training coordinator to recommend one training plan for the twenty seasonal designers and to say how that plan will be explained to the senior designers it falls on.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: Who does this land hardest on?
How would you explain it to them?
